title: AnalyteCatalog
description: The app's reference data, schema 1: the analyte catalog in web/public/data/analyses.json, plus the two panel layers it is composed into — the laboratory groups in panels.json (referenced as #/$defs/labPanel) and the product's Monitoring Panels in monitoring-panels.json (#/$defs/monitoringPanel). The catalog is the single source of truth for everything the app knows about a LOINC code, so every fact about a code — its names (including its short name), its expected unit, the further units accepted for it, and whether it is a variant of another code — lives on one entry here and nowhere in TypeScript. Unlike the interchange envelope, this is app-internal data with no outside authors and no forward-compatibility promise: the objects are therefore CLOSED, so a mistyped key fails the conformance suite instead of being silently ignored at runtime.

loinc.description: A LOINC code in its printed form: digits, a hyphen, then the check digit. The same shape the parser validates uploaded observations against, which is what keeps a lab-internal code like "900101" out of the catalog.

lang.description: Translations keyed by BCP 47 tag. English is not a key here: it is the `friendlyName`/`name` field itself, so an entry can never carry a translation without carrying the original.

analyte.title: Analyte
analyte.description: One LOINC code the app knows about. Present in the catalog means the LOINC cross-check may derive this code from a printed name, so an entry is added when the product genuinely measures the analyte — not as a place to park a label.

longCommonName.description: Required. LOINC's own long common name, verbatim — the authority on what the code means, shown in the UI as the "LOINC name". The cross-check's grey line under a printed name shows friendlyName, not this.

friendlyName.description: Required. The friendly name: the clinical name the app prints. Short enough for a table cell, unlike longCommonName.

shortName.description: Optional. The app's own short name, shown on badges in Monitoring Panels and All Observations ("HbA1c", "TSH"). Ours, NOT LOINC's own SHORTNAME field. Absent means the app falls back to friendlyName, so a code carries one only where an abbreviation is genuinely what a reader looks for. Requires `unit`: a short name without a reference unit could not be range-checked.
shortName.$comment: Was SHORT_LABELS in markers.ts; read as SHORT_NAMES in analyteCatalog.ts.

unit.description: Optional. The unit this code is expected in, as printed rather than in UCUM. A LOINC fixes the kind of quantity but not the scale, so this is what lets a row's unit pick the right variant of a multi-code analyte. Absent means the app knows nothing about the code's units and never checks a printed unit's dimension against the code.

allowedUnits.description: Optional. Further units accepted for this code beyond `unit` — LOINC's own example units for 1848-1 (DHT) list both ng/dL and pg/mL. The validation warning fires only for a unit whose dimension matches neither `unit` nor any unit in this set; another scale of the same quantity raises nothing.

aliasOf.description: Optional. The primary code this entry is a unit or method variant of. The primary owns the row, the short name and the chart series; a result uploaded under this code folds into it. Must name an entry that is not itself an alias.

aliasLabel.description: Optional. How this variant differs from its primary, in the words shown on the chip beside the row: "nmol/L unit", "whole blood", "IFCC unit". Meaningless without `aliasOf`.

analyteInfo.title: AnalyteInfo
analyteInfo.description: The prose the marker popup shows. Optional throughout: a code the app can chart is useful long before anyone has written about it.

lang.description: Per-language overrides of the fields above. A language may translate only some of them.

labPanel.title: LabPanel
labPanel.description: One laboratory group: the way a lab orders and prints a set of analytes ("Full Blood Count", "Lipid Metabolism"). This layer describes the laboratory's world, not the product's — Monitoring Panels are composed over it. A group states its LOINCs either flat in `loincs` or split into printed `sections`, never both.

id.description: Required. Stable slug a Monitoring Panel definition refers to by `panelId`/`panelIds`.

iconOld.description: The inline SVG this group's icon used before it became a file. Kept as provenance.

monitoringPanel.title: MonitoringPanel
monitoringPanel.description: One card in the Monitoring Panels grid: the product's own grouping, expressed as a composition over the laboratory groups. Exactly one source of LOINCs — `panelId`, `panelIds` or a literal `loincs` — then `excludeLoincs` drops what the clinical question does not need and `extraLoincs` pulls in what it does, in that order. Array order here is the order the cards render in.

name.description: Required. The card's title, and the key computed indices name their panels by.

panelId.description: Take every LOINC from this one laboratory group.

panelIds.description: Take every LOINC from these laboratory groups, concatenated in order. Two or more — a single group is `panelId`.

loincs.description: State the starting LOINCs outright, for a panel no single laboratory group corresponds to.

excludeLoincs.description: Dropped from the LOINCs taken above, before `extraLoincs` is appended. Needed even for a code that has an `aliasOf` primary in the panel: the grid resolves LOINCs one-to-one and does not fold aliases, so an unexcluded variant would render its own second row.

extraLoincs.description: Appended after exclusion — the analytes this clinical question needs that the laboratory group does not order together.
